issues.description: Existing candidate CAND-00006 ('High-Level Overview') captures the need for a high-level overview of all branches' capacity but omits the source's explicit mention that the overview should surface 'key metrics' in the summary view.
issues.suggested_fix: Expand candidate CAND-00006 to mention that the high-level/summary view must present key metrics (as requested by stakeholders) — e.g., include wording such as 'high-level summary view showing all branches and key metrics' and reference the source evidence.

issues.description: Independent review discovered CAND-00276: The capacity overview should support grouping or aggregation of locations (for example by system or region) or provide aggregated/summarized views to avoid overcrowded displays when many branches are present.
issues.suggested_fix: Integrate this new grounded candidate, merging only if semantically equivalent.

issues.description: Independent review discovered CAND-00277: The capacity interface should support operational planning (for example: deciding where to move items or allocate resources) by presenting the 'big picture' across branches so managers can use the overview to make redistribution/allocation decisions.
issues.suggested_fix: Integrate this new grounded candidate, merging only if semantically equivalent.

issues.description: CAND-00011 (Shelf Space Usage Report) omits an explicit requirement present in the source: branch managers must be able to see their local situation AND see how they compare to the system average. Source literal quote: "This way branch managers can see their local situation AND see how they compare to the system average." The existing candidate requires per-library and per-system reports and side-by-side comparisons across libraries, but it does not explicitly require a system-average comparison metric or presentation that makes the system-average visible alongside a branch's results.
issues.suggested_fix: Amend CAND-00011 to explicitly require the shelf-space report to present a system-average comparative value (for example: a system-average column/row, an overlay, or an explicit 'compare to system average' view) so branch managers can directly compare local percentages to the system-wide average. Document how the system average is calculated (scope, inclusion rules) and how it is displayed in side-by-side or comparison views.

issues.description: The existing candidate CAND-00038 (Batch Status Conversion) records the need for a batch status-conversion report/utility but omits operational and safety details that the source explicitly and repeatedly raised for batch operations. The email thread requested bulk status changes (example: changing 100 items at once) while several respondents warned about safety (avoid accidental mass changes) and asked for the same protections required for destructive purging workflows.
issues.suggested_fix: Augment CAND-00038 to include the safety and operational controls expected for bulk operations: require a preview step with a concise human-readable summary (number of items, source status(es), target status, scope), an explicit confirmation action before applying changes, an auditable log entry for every applied batch-status change (operator id, timestamp, affected item ids, source and target statuses, optional reason), and an undo/rollback capability or a documented configurable undo window and known limitations. For large selections require chunked processing with progress reporting and retry/resume semantics, and require role-based permission controls and a separate confirmation/authorization step for bulk status changes that could affect large percentages of a branch/system collection.

issues.description: The candidate CAND-00039 ('Last Copy Report') is present but its captured wording focuses on the 'library system's last copies' and does not preserve the source's explicit request for both per-library (branch) and per-system views. Thomas and others explicitly asked for both scoped views and Robert described the detection rule ('for each item record, is this the only copy in the specified scope? If yes, flag it').
issues.suggested_fix: Update CAND-00039 to explicitly require both scope options (per-library/branch and per-system) and to document the precise detection logic: for each item record, evaluate whether any other copies exist within the selected scope (branch or system); if none exist, flag the item as a last copy. Also require that the report expose bibliographic identifiers and exportable context to support catalogers (as the draft's Item-purging requirement notes), and document how scope selection affects flags and any caching/replication semantics that might delay last-copy detection.

issues.description: The source explicitly requests that, at the system level, staff be able to see which branches have the most inactive patrons (a ranked/aggregated breakdown by home library). The draft captures scoping (System/Home Library/County) but does not explicitly require aggregated counts or ranking by branch when run at system scope.
issues.suggested_fix: Add a requirement that inactive-patron reports, when executed at system scope, provide aggregated counts grouped by home library and support ranking/sorting (for example: 'top N branches by inactive-patron count') and include those group-level aggregates in exported outputs.

issues.description: The source requests the ability to assign cleanup tasks from a home-library scoped view of the inactive-patrons report so branch-level staff can be assigned work. The draft does not include any requirement for creating or recording such assignments from the report UI or export workflow.
issues.suggested_fix: Add a requirement that home-library scoped inactive-patron reports support creating or recording cleanup assignments (for example: assign to branch or staff, set an optional due date and status) or integrate with the existing export/workflow mechanism so assignments created from the report are tracked and auditable.

issues.description: Independent review discovered CAND-00278: At the system level, the report must provide aggregated counts and allow ranking/grouping by home library/branch so operators can see which branches have the most inactive patrons.
issues.suggested_fix: Integrate this new grounded candidate, merging only if semantically equivalent.

issues.description: Independent review discovered CAND-00279: When run at a Home Library scope, the inactive-patrons report must support creating or assigning cleanup tasks (for example: assign a branch or staff responsibility, and record that assignment) so branch staff can be given specific cleanup work based on the report.
issues.suggested_fix: Integrate this new grounded candidate, merging only if semantically equivalent.

issues.description: The specification requires that the reporting subsystem 'must operate in read-only mode with respect to OPAC data' while the source text states only that management-process requirements 'must not constrain functionality or features of the OPAC module.' The introduced 'read-only' constraint is a change in scope (it forbids management-process writes even where original text did not explicitly do so).
issues.suggested_fix: Either remove the added 'read-only' prohibition or justify and cite stakeholder intent for read-only behavior. If read-only behavior is required, rephrase to reference the source (for example: 'reports must not modify OPAC behavior; where reporting updates are needed, they must be explicitly documented and allowed only with administrator consent').

issues.description: The specification adds a normative prohibition against denormalized reporting schemas ('avoid denormalized schemas that fight the relational model') whereas the source requires only a 'fully relational database back-end.' The added strict prohibition may unnecessarily constrain legitimate reporting-warehouse designs.
issues.suggested_fix: Rephrase as a non-normative design preference or clarify scope: allow denormalized schemas in separate reporting/warehouse contexts if justified for performance, but document the preferred relational approach and any interoperability expectations.

issues.description: The original document explicitly says front-line staff should not be able to alter templates to display deleted items (example in the report-templates discussion). That precise protective constraint is not present in the draft specification's Report Templates / permissions text.
issues.suggested_fix: Incorporate the explicit prohibition from the source: require template restrictions (configurable by administrators) that prevent templates available to front-line staff from exposing deleted records or other restricted data fields. Add a normative sentence that templates intended for front-line staff must not allow enabling display of deleted or purged records unless an administrator with appropriate privilege explicitly grants that capability.

issues.description: Independent review discovered CAND-00280: For example, front-line staff could set a call number range for a weeding report or add/remove display fields from a pick list, but they should not be able to alter the template to display deleted items.
issues.suggested_fix: Integrate this new grounded candidate, merging only if semantically equivalent.

issues.description: The source includes an explicit example constraining what template-modifying staff may change: "Front-line staff can set a call number range for a weeding report or add/remove display fields from a pick list, but can't alter the template to display deleted items." The draft accepts a general requirement that "admins should be able to limit which filters and display fields can be altered" (CAND-00133) but does not preserve this explicit example or the specific prohibition against enabling display of deleted items. That particular restriction is a concrete operational safety/control example that implementers and administrators may reasonably expect to see represented in template-permission rules or examples.
issues.suggested_fix: Augment the Report Templates candidate (CAND-00133) or its explanatory text to preserve the source example and make explicit whether administrators MUST be able to prevent cloned/modified templates from exposing deleted-item state (for example: an admin-configurable block on display of deleted/lapsed records). If the intention was only illustrative, note that the example is illustrative; if it is a required control, add an explicit statement such as: "Administrators shall be able to prevent templates and cloned templates from exposing deleted items or other sensitive status fields (for example via a deny-list of display fields), and the UI must make these protected fields visible to admins when authoring templates."

issues.description: The document's explicit list of canned/pre-defined reports (Section 2.2) is not represented in the draft requirements. Multiple discrete canned report names from DOC-014 (Checkout Count; Renewals Count; Non-Cataloged Count; Circulation Count by Shelving Location; Items Added Count; Items Deleted Count; Items Currently Checked Out; Items Overdue by X Days; Bib Records Count; Bib Records with No Volumes Attached; Patron Count; Patron Count by Home Library; Bills Currently Owed by Patrons; Detailed Payments Received) are present in the source text but are not captured as candidates or mapped to requirements in the draft.
issues.suggested_fix: Add explicit functional requirements (or map to existing requirements) to cover each canned report named in DOC-014's Section 2.2, or include a clear statement that those specific canned reports are intentionally excluded/covered elsewhere with precise references. At minimum, preserve the source's enumerated canned-report names as delivered-template expectations or as examples in the 'canned reports' requirement.

issues.description: DOC-014 lists a limitation 'No ability to check multiple reports to run at the same time' under report-scheduling limitations. The draft requirements add scheduling and queue features but do not explicitly require a capability to select/check multiple reports and submit them to run simultaneously (batch-start of multiple report definitions).
issues.suggested_fix: If 'ability to select multiple reports to run at the same time' is a desired operational capability, add an explicit functional requirement to the report-scheduling/queueing area describing the expected UI/behavior (for example: multi-select in scheduling UI, submit-as-batch, per-report recipients and scheduling metadata, and queue semantics for batch submissions). If not desired, explicitly document that DOC-014's limitation was considered and intentionally not pursued.

Omitting these makes the historical context from DOC-014 harder to trace.
issues.suggested_fix: Include DOC-014's explicit deployment facts (Evergreen version 1.4.0.4; 'approximately 3.5 million patrons'; 'collection of 9.6 million items') in the specification's deployment/operational-assumptions section, or reference DOC-014 explicitly where those facts are recorded so implementers retain the original historical context.

issues.description: Candidate CAND-00147 ('Track Uncataloged Material') appears in the draft but several distinct operational details from the source interview were not preserved. The interview named additional, actionable constraints that shape the required workflow: quick distribution ('we need to process these fast'), minimal branch labor ('we can't spend a lot of time per item'), explicit ability to identify how the material is being used, and the need to count those transactions so they are included in circulation statistics and reports. Those details are present in the source but are not represented in the candidate's recorded statement or in the corresponding requirement text.
issues.suggested_fix: Augment the Uncataloged-material requirement (and/or CAND-00147) to explicitly include the interview's constraints: (a) support rapid distribution/processing (low per-item handling time), (b) minimize branch labor (a minimal-labor workflow), (c) capture/use metrics that let staff identify how uncataloged items are being used, and (d) ensure transactions for uncataloged items are counted and folded into circulation statistics and reports. Include the literal source wording in the requirement text for traceability (e.g. quote: 'quick distribution (we need to process these fast), minimal branch labor (we can't spend a lot of time per item), and ability to identify how the material is being used. We also need to count transactions and include them in circulation statistics and reports.').

issues.description: The draft specification adds an explicit read-only prohibition for reporting against OPAC data ("reporting subsystem shall operate in read-only mode with respect to OPAC data: it may query or replicate OPAC-created data but must not modify OPAC data or state"). The meeting minutes state only that management processes should not constrain OPAC functionality or patron access; they do not explicitly require that reporting components be forbidden from making any writes. The draft therefore imposes a stronger constraint than DOC-018's source text supports.
issues.suggested_fix: Either remove or reword the absolute 'read-only' prohibition (if undesired), or add a provenance note citing a source that requires read-only behavior. If the intent is to prevent user-facing disruption, prefer wording that requires architectural separation and non-disruptiveness (background processing, replicas, transaction isolation) rather than an absolute ban on writes unless another source mandates it.

issues.description: The Batch item transfer utility requirement in the draft lists DOC-019 as one of its sources, but the supplied source document (DOC-019 meeting notes) contains no discussion of batch item-transfer utilities, transfer-preview/undo mechanics, scheduling/revert semantics, transfer logging, chunked processing, selection UX (multi-select, select-all, persistent selection), barcode/TCN uploads, or the other detailed behaviors attributed to that requirement. Attributing these detailed batch-transfer requirements to DOC-019 is therefore false provenance.
issues.suggested_fix: Remove DOC-019 from the provenance for the batch-item-transfer-related candidate IDs unless supporting text can be added to DOC-019; alternatively, add a precise citation to the actual source document(s) that substantiate each batch-transfer sub-requirement.

issues.description: Shelf-space reporting appears twice: the canonical Shelf-space utilization report in the requirements set and a candidate Shelf Space Usage Report (CAND-00011). This duplication can cause confusion in implementation and documentation; consolidate into a single canonical requirement.
issues.suggested_fix: Merge into one canonical shelf-space reporting requirement and map all references to that single definition; remove or rename duplicates accordingly.

issues.description: Two separate candidates describe an item batch transfer utility (CAND-00016 and CAND-00098) that appear to cover the same functionality. This duplication can lead to inconsistent implementation details across modules.
issues.suggested_fix: Select one canonical description for the batch item transfer utility and remove the redundant candidate; unify terminology and scope.

issues.description: Inactive-patrons reporting and outreach export is described by many candidate statements (CAND-00059, CAND-00060, CAND-00061, CAND-00062, CAND-00063, CAND-00058, CAND-00065, CAND-00103, CAND-00236, CAND-00259). This represents a cross-document duplication of the same capability across multiple entries.
issues.suggested_fix: Redefine a single canonical inactive-patrons reporting requirement and consolidate all related candidates under it with explicit mapping.

issues.description: Data quality and bibliographic integrity reporting is duplicated: canonical data-quality intent vs candidate CAND-00158. This can cause divergent scope or field mappings during implementation.
issues.suggested_fix: Consolidate into a single canonical data-quality/bibliographic integrity requirement and map all related candidates to it.

issues.description: Open-template reporting and related query tooling appear with multiple names (open-template, query tool, etc.) across candidates (CAND-00119, CAND-00132, CAND-00081). This can create confusion about what is exposed in each mode.
issues.suggested_fix: Standardize terminology and clearly differentiate canned, on-demand, and open-template interfaces with distinct IDs and descriptions.

issues.description: Board/executive reporting artifacts appear under multiple candidates (CAND-00117, CAND-00135, CAND-00085, CAND-00086). This may fragment governance-oriented requirements for board reports.
issues.suggested_fix: Consolidate into a single canonical board/executive reporting item and reference all related templates from that entry.

issues.description: Blacklist entries present in the ledger (CAND-00169, CAND-00170, CAND-00171, CAND-00172, CAND-00178) describe governance tasks (reports governance, testing groups, etc.) rather than runtime software requirements.
issues.suggested_fix: Move these governance-related items to project/governance artifacts and keep the runtime requirements ledger focused on implementable software obligations.

issues.description: Shelf-space terminology inconsistency (Shelf-space vs Shelf Space) across the canonical requirement and candidate CAND-00011.
issues.suggested_fix: Choose a single term (e.g., Shelf-space utilization report) and align all references to that term.

issues.description: Cross-document proliferation of near-same capabilities (e.g., various reporting interfaces, historical vs real-time, etc.) suggests lack of a unified capability map in the current ledger. This increases risk of gaps or overlaps during implementation.
issues.suggested_fix: Create a canonical capability catalog and map each candidate to a single entry; explicitly deduplicate overlapping candidates where appropriate.

issues.description: CAND-00168 / missing_detail: The entry captures an online, hierarchical, cross-linked HTML help system but does not explicitly preserve the candidate's usability requirements that the help be searchable and 'easy to navigate'. Those are material user-facing qualifiers affecting findability and usability of help content.
issues.suggested_fix: Extend the requirement language to explicitly require the online HTML help to be searchable and to be organized/navigation-designed for ease-of-use (for example: include full-text search, index, table of contents, clear breadcrumbing and cross-links), and indicate where search results and navigation affordances appear in the UI.

issues.description: CAND-00169 / unsupported: The candidate describes working-group mission/governance and project activities (documenting functionality, testing-group duties, compiling lists) rather than a runtime software requirement. The source is a meeting motion prescribing group tasks, not an operational obligation the software must implement.
issues.suggested_fix: Record these items in project governance or project-plan artifacts (working-group charter, test-plan, roadmap) rather than in the software requirements document; if any runtime capability is intended (for example a report-authoring/testing workflow), express that as a concrete software requirement with traceable user stories and acceptance criteria.

issues.description: CAND-00170 / unsupported: This candidate is a project-role/task assignment (become the Reports testing group) and does not specify a software behavior or capability required of the product. Rejecting it as a software requirement is consistent with the source intent.
issues.suggested_fix: Move this governance/task to project-management documentation. If a software capability is desired (for example: a mechanism to manage report test cases or filter new report builds through a testing workflow), specify that functionality explicitly (UI, permissions, workflow states, audit trail).

issues.description: CAND-00171 / unsupported: The candidate requests compilation of a list of reports needed for an Executive Reports Interface — a project deliverable/analysis task rather than a software runtime obligation. The requirements entry appropriately treated this as out-of-scope for software requirements.
issues.suggested_fix: Capture as a product-management or working-group deliverable. If a software obligation is intended (pre-delivered executive report templates), specify the exact templates, fields and schedule requirements to be included with the product.

issues.description: CAND-00172 / unsupported: Determining and creating templates for PINES libraries is a project-authoring task, not a direct software runtime requirement. The specification should not mandate project work items as software capabilities.
issues.suggested_fix: If the intended software obligation is to ship a set of delivered templates, convert this governance task into a concrete requirement listing which templates will be delivered and their fields/permissions; otherwise track the activity in project planning artifacts.

issues.description: CAND-00178 / unsupported: The candidate prescribes an iterative, prototype-oriented methodology for UI specification — this is a recommended design process, not a declarative software behavior. Treating it as a software requirement is a category error; the source intent is process/methodology guidance.
issues.suggested_fix: Move the item into project/process documentation (design approach). If any runtime deliverable is expected (for example: deliver interactive UI prototypes with specified screens), express those as concrete deliverables with acceptance criteria and trace them as requirements.

issues.description: CAND-00261 / missing_detail: The quoted source text only lists "Holds Purchase Alert (not available)" with no supporting detail. The assigned paragraph adds many concrete behaviors (criteria examples, operator-configurable thresholds, per-branch/system scope, export formats, schedulable background job, and documentation about behavior when acquisitions/EDI data are absent) that are not present in the supplied evidence or listed as other supporting candidates for this pair. Therefore the paragraph asserts material qualifiers and behaviors not supported by the single-line source.
issues.suggested_fix: Either (A) reduce the paragraph to the obligation that is directly supported by the quote (e.g. “The system shall provide a Holds Purchase Alert report”), and link/merge additional behavior (configurable criteria, scheduling, scope, export formats, and handling of missing acquisitions/EDI data) to other specific supporting candidates (for example CAND-00116 for holds-report types, and vendor/EDI candidates) before keeping them in the paragraph; or (B) add the specific other_supporting_evidence candidate IDs that justify each added detail (thresholds, per-branch scope, export formats, background scheduling, and documentation behavior) so the detailed clauses are traceable to source evidence.
